title: Principality of Ryazan
capsule: The Principality of Ryazan was a northeastern Rus' principality centered on the city of Ryazan (Old Ryazan, south of the present-day city) on the Oka River, separated from Murom in the mid-twelfth century and thereafter frequently in conflict with its larger neighbor Vladimir-Suzdal. Ryazan's princes pursued an independent foreign policy and resisted Vladimiran dominance, but the principality was the first major Rus' entity to be struck by the Mongol invasion: in December 1237 Batu Khan's forces destroyed Old Ryazan utterly, killing its prince Yuri Igorevich and most of the population, an event commemorated in the literary Tale of the Destruction of Ryazan. The principality's successor state relocated its center to Pereyaslavl-Ryazansky (the current Ryazan), surviving as a Mongol vassal until its absorption into the Muscovite state in 1521.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The principality's core territory on the Oka is reasonably attested; its shifting eastern and southern boundaries against steppe peoples are incompletely documented.
